INTRODUCTION
      I, the Chairman of the Department-related Parliamentary Standing Committee on Science & Technology, Environment
 & Forests, having been authorised by the Committee to present the Report on its behalf, present this One Hundred-
Seventeenth Report of the Committee. This Report deals with the detailed Demands for Grants (2003-2004) of the
 Department of Science & Technology (Demand No.80).
 
2.  In the meeting of the Committee held on the 31
st March, 2003 the Secretary and other Officers of the Department of
 Science & Technology gave an overview of the various activities of the Department and the Members sought
 clarifications on various aspects of the performance of the Department to enable it to scrutinise the Demands for Grants.
 
3.  The Committee expresses its thanks to the Officers of the Department for replying to the clarifications sought by the
 Members and placing before it the required material to enable the Committee to scrutinise the Demands for Grants of the
 Department of Science & Technology.
 
4.         The Committee considered and adopted the Report at its meeting held on  29
th April, 2003.
 
NEW DELHI
April 29  , 2003
C. RAMACHANDRAIAH
Chairman
Committee on Science & Technology,
Environment & Forests.
 
      
REPORT
Indian tradition of pursuing science and science related activities dates back to thousands and thousands of years. 
 After we attained independence the Government accorded top priority to science and scientific research.  Prime Minister
 Jawaharlal Nehru described our planning process as nothing but science in action.  He declared that “It is science alone
 that could solve the problems of hunger and poverty”.   In spite of resource constraints India’s success in the fields of
 science and technology is spectacular.
To give a direction to the promotion of Science and Technology the Department of Science and Technology was
 established with the primary objective of promoting new areas of Science and Technology and to play the role of a nodal
 department for organising, co-ordinating and promoting S&T activities in the country.  The mandate given to DST
 include, among others:
Ø      Formulation of policy statements and guidelines on S&T
Ø      Promotion of new areas of scientific research
Ø      Co-ordination of inter-departmental S&T efforts
Ø      Support basic and applied research in universities and other institutions
International S&T Co-operation

 Setting up a Patent Facilitating Cell to provide support to scientists and technologists on all aspects of patenting.

BUDGETARY ALLOCATION
4.         The Department of Science and Technology has been allocated Rs.1176.12 crores (Rs.790.00 plan and Rs.386.12
 crores non-plan) for the year 2003-2004. It was informed that the Planning Commission made a Plan allocation of
 Rs.800.00 crores for the year 2003-2004 out of which Rs.10.00 crores are proposed to be transferred to the Ministry of
 Urban Development for incorporation in the Budget document of that Ministry, for Capital Works to be executed during
 2003-2004.
The increase in Plan provision of 2003-2004 as compared to R.E 2002-2003 is mainly due to increased allocations
 for Research & Development support – up from Rs.210.00 crores to Rs.215.00 crores; outlay for Technology for Bamboo
 Products has been increased from Rs.20.00 crores to Rs.43.25 crores; India Metrological Department Rs,60.00 crores as
 against Rs.55.00 crores; and for two new schemes Pharmaceutical Research & Development Support Fund – Rs.150.00
 crores and Rs.10.00 crores for Synergy Projects, a scheme which is to be operated by the Office of the Principal Scientific
 Adviser to the Government of India. The compounding allocation of the B.E. and R.E. stages for the two years are as
 given below:

 during B.E and R.E stage in the year 2002-03 were provided for the Regional Sophisticated Instrument Facilities and

FUND FOR IMPROVEMENT OF S&T INFRASTRUCTURE IN UNIVERSITIES AND OTHER HIGHER
 EDUCATIONAL INSTITUTIONS (FIST)
           
7.         The Committee was informed that the objective of this initiative is to strengthen R&D infrastructure in the
 Academic/Research Institutions. It would identify active University/Academic Departments through a peer review
 mechanism including on-site visits and the funding would be done at two levels.   The scheme would provide basic
 infrastructure and facilities for promoting R&D in new and emerging fields of S&T which would also help in attracting
 fresh talent in such Departments.  The proposals supported under the programme would be monitored annually or bi-
annually through an appropriate mechanism.
8.         It was informed that they also plan to invite fresh applications from the prospective Departments/Centres of the
 Universities/academic institutions sometime in July-August 2003 for supporting under the Program and an allocation of
 about Rs.35-40 crores required to extend support to the freshly recommended proposals in year 2003-04.
            The progress of departments who have received the support under the Programme will also be monitored   &
 reviewed by visit of the Expert Member along with the Presentation by the department.
9.            Financial support to the 25 Proposals under Level – II category has also been provided.  Support is also extended
 for continuation of already supported cases in both levels I & II for remaining Equipment grants, Networking &
 Computational facility, Infrastructure Facility and Maintenance and to carry out these activities so far about Rs.35 Crores
 have been utilized.
10.       The Committee notes with constraint that the quality of infrastructure available in our Universities and research
 laboratories for pursuing scientific research is not upto the  mark.  Lack of interest on the part of students to go for science
 education is indeed alarming.    The Department is taking steps to encourage young scientists to pursue serious scientific
 work.  The Committee notes with concern the decline of the quality of our research papers.  There is an urgent need to
 take concerted efforts to arrest this trend to give new dynamism and momentum to Indian science.   
SCIENCE & TECHNOLOGY FOR WOMEN
11.       Women form a very important part of the national scientific workforce.  Indian science requires induction of more
 women scientists and technologists to improve the quality of science and its application towards national development.
 Women face special problems due to their
duties towards motherhood and family and, most of them, suffer “break in their careers” due to these responsibilities.  
 There has been a long-felt need to have special schemes to revive their professional careers.
12.       The Committee was informed that through the scheme ‘Science and Technology for Women’ support is provided
 to time bound action-research projects designed to reduce drudgery, provide newer opportunities for income generation
 based on local resources, address problems pertaining to women’s health and nutrition including occupational health. 
 Successful technology packages are then replicated to field test the model through coordinated programmes.  The
 Department also provides support for the setting up of rural Women’s Technology Parks to showcase technology
 packages relevant to the area, provide technical and entrepreneurial training to women and interface with S&T institutions
 to address specific problems faced by women.
13.       The Government of India, in keeping with its commitment towards welfare and empowerment of women, has come
 up with a special and innovative new scheme which  envisages support to woman scientists, with or without a break in
 career, to pursue science in all its aspects and encourage them to continue in the scientific profession and also to
 contribute towards application of science and technology to societal development.  Approximately 100 scholarships a year
 will be awarded in the specialized subject areas. It is also interesting to report that the women scientists have showed an
 overwhelming response for the scheme. Approximately 5000 women scientists have already approached the department
 for support under this scheme.
14.       Women Scientists Scheme will provide opportunities to women scientists and technologists between the age group
 of 30-50 years.  Under this scheme, women scientists will be provided attractive financial support to pursue research in
 frontier areas of science and engineering, on societal problems requiring S&T intervention and for receiving training for
 possible self-employment in S&T related services sector.
15.       The Women Scientists Scheme (Part-B) to encourage women scientists to take up research on societal problems

REPORT

 was also widely advertised and about 150 applications have been received.  An Expert Committee has also been set up
 which is screening the proposals.              The Women Scientists (Part-C) designed to prepare women scientists to
 undertake self-entrepreneurship has also been advertised and the selection process is on. 
16.       The Committee appreciates the Department for launching a new Scheme for women and hopes that with the
 introduction of the Scholarships, the contribution of women to science & technology would increase.   The Committee
 recommends that the Department may specially focus on rural women.  The aim should also be to tap the potential of
 women in smaller towns who because of lack of financial support  or infrastructure do not pursue science studies.
SPECIAL COMPONENT PLAN FOR SCHEDULED CASTES
17.       The Department informed the Committee that a special plan was undertaken with a view to promoting research,
 development and adaptation of technology for improving the quality of life of the economically weaker sections of
 scheduled castes in urban/rural areas; to encourage scientists & technologists to apply their knowledge and expertise to
 the needs of
economically weaker scheduled caste communities, specially in rural areas and to promote activities such as workshops,
 publications, jathas, etc.
18.       The Department further informed that based on the past experience gained during implementation of projects they
 propose to encourage and develop coordinated programme on scientific rearing of smaller animals and poultry birds and
 management of organic waste.  Some of the exclusive artisanal trades such as carcass collection and processing, footwear
 making, masonary, etc.  will be accorded priority and at the same time individual projects on creating awareness,
 developing the capability of SC community as also the training programme will also continue.   It is also proposed to
 undertake projects on alternative vocations in the SC pockets where chances of income generation and creation of
 employment are dwindling.  Entrepreneurial skill development will be an important input in our efforts.  Motivated
 engineers and scientists from community poly-techniques and engineering colleges will be encouraged to contribute to
 finding of technical solutions to urban SC populations.
19.       When the Committee wanted to know about the activities undertaken under this scheme it was informed that the
 Department encouraged S&T Institutes & NGOs to undertake innovative and adaptive tasks for the benefit of tribal/SC
 communities.  Broad areas of activities included innovative technology development and functional capability/skill
 development and training in technology areas such as sustainable agriculture, agro-forestry, cover management, natural
 resources regeneration, health, water, medicinal plants, artisanal sector, animal husbandry, post harvest technologies in the
 rural sector and new income generating programmes in the urban sector.  Apart from individual projects on research
 development and adaptation of relevant technologies, coordinated programmes based on the outcome of pilot
 development projects were initiated for large-scale field testing and demonstration.    The scheme is being restructured to
 avoid possible overlap with schemes being implemented by other Departments/agencies.
20.       The Committee hopes that this programme would aim at providing alternate vocation as well as additional income
 to these communities.  The programmes should also aim at uplifting their social status.  These communities mostly are not
 aware of these programmes.   By giving due publicity to such programmes the Department can reach out to the lowest 
 rungs of these communities and sensitise them about the benefits of such schemes for improving their living conditions
 and for their empowerment.   The I & B Ministry is willing to cooperate in the direction and it should be tapped without
 delay.
PATENT FACILITATING CENTRE (PFC)
21.       The Committee was informed that Patent Facilitating Centre has been engaged in many activities related to
 intellectual property rights (IPR) with an objective to introduce patent information as a vital input in the process of
 promotion of R&D programmes; provide patenting facilities to scientists and technologists of the country for Indian and
 foreign patents on a sustained basis; keep a watch on developments in the area of IPR and make important issues known
 to policy makers, scientists, industrialists and others  create awareness and understanding relating to patents and the
 challenges and opportunities in the area; undertake study and analysis of policy related and operational matters emanating
 from the TRIPs agreement and other agreements under the World Trade Organisaton and to act as a focal point in this
 matter within DST.
22.       It was informed that during the year 2002-2003 PFC has organised 45 patent awareness workshops and sensitised
 about 5000 scientists, technologists and policy makers, with a total number of 186 workshops conducted so far. PFC also
 conducted a two-day workshop for the Mauritius Research Council in Mauritius.  PFC has facilitated filing of 40 patent
 applications so far, which included 21 applications filed in India, 7 in USA and 7 PCT applications and four US patents

 were granted during this period.
23.       It was also informed that PFC plans to open more Patent Information Centres towards the goal of having one PIC
 in each state. PFC shall continue organising patent awareness workshops, training programmes, bringing out the monthly
 bulletin on IPR, patent databases on Indian patents Ekaswa and facilitating filing of patent applications in India and
 abroad. It also plans to bring out the upgraded version of video on patents in view of the latest amendments in the Patents
 Act.  A new software is being developed for Ekaswa A and B for providing more information at a quicker speed. Other
 activities include providing advisory and consultancy services to industry, universities, R&D institutions; undertaking
 research and futuristic studies on IPR related topics and organising international workshops.
24.       When the Committee wanted to know about the progress made in setting up of Patent Facilitating Centre in various
 States and the budgetary allocation made in this regard it was informed that thirteen Patent Information centres
 (PICs)have been so far set up in 13 States, namely Andhra Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, Gujarat, Himachal Pradesh, Kerala,
 Madhya Pradesh, Manipur, Punjab, Rajasthan, Sikkim, Uttar Pradesh, Uttaranchal and West Bengal. PICs in Assam and
 Tripura would be set up soon. They have decided to continue the PICs, which have completed 5 years, during 10
th plan. It
 is estimated that Rs.4 crores will be needed for PICs in all States for 5 years. It was also informed that additional
 budgetary allocation would be made to setup PICs in all the States and have them running for 5 years.
25.       The Committee notes that patent literacy will promote greater awareness and knowledge among people and enable
 them to make informed choices.  To safeguard our germplasm and traditional knowledge and to assert our right to own
 our genetic diversity knowledge about patenting is indispensable.   Patenting of Haldee and Basmati abroad and our
 successful fight against those patents is a clear pointer towards adopting greater vigilance for protecting our biodiversity.  
 The Committee recommends that the Department may augment its own efforts in this regard and give due publicity to
 such activities for the benefit of scientists, researchers and the general public.   After all to save our traditional knowledge
 we will not only depend on scientific community but also on women, rural folk and people and individuals.     
JOINT TECHNOLOGY PROGRAMME
26.       The Committee was informed that the objective of the programme is to provide specific support for activities
 which are conducive to strengthening technological capabilities in the country.  It also aims at applying high technology
 for Water Purification, Noise Abatement, learning Enhancement, etc. This programme also funds multi-disciplinary
 core/critical areas like IPM, Molecular electronics/Biosensors, Micro & Nano-materials & Nano-structures, Imaging
 Systems, Value addition & applications/studies, New Information & Communication Technology & Applications, Laser
 Technologies and Applications, etc.  The modernisation of traditional technologies, tools and skills for a few selected
 areas;  Enhancing Export capabilities
and performance of the traditional/non-traditional items; funding to R&D Applications activities in North-Eastern region
 and providing support to ongoing projects under CTP/NSP scheme of DST – till their successful completion are also the
 objectives of the scheme in the year 2003.
27.       The Committee was informed that the Department in the year 2003-04 would undertake the following activities
 under this scheme. These include:- 
i)             Initiation of development of Arsenic Removal and Fluoride removal Technology Systems.
ii)            Biosensors & Molecular Electronics projects for pesticide detection etc.
iii)             Superconducting Technologies & Application Demonstrations.
iv)         Waste utilisation, recycling & management projects.
v)             Support to ongoing projects in the areas of brain computer interface, DNA    based     electronic devices etc.
vi)         Glass Design studio to enable use of glass as medium for creative arts.
vii)
               Design fabrication and standardization of a high precision fibre optical sensor  for   instant determination of
 adulteration in petrol.
viii)       State-of-art  optical surveying equipment, development of protective biocompatible coating on surgical tools.
ix)         Design and development of night driving filters – Phase-II and design and development of precision aspheric
 lenses for indirect  ophthalmoscope and,
x)          Setting up of NML-DST Hall –Marking facility based upon ICP-OES technique at  Jamshedpur.
28.       While the Committee notes with satisfaction that the Department is engaged in producing and applying

INTERNATIONAL ADVANCED RESEARCH CENTRE FOR POWDER METALLURGY AND NEW MATERIALS,
 (ARCI)
29.       The Committee was informed that ARCI was setup with a specific mandate to acquire materials-based technologies
 of possible interest to Indian industries, from CIS countries like, Russia, Ukraine, Belarus, Uzbekhistan, Moldava, etc.  
 While this mandate has been implemented rather satisfactorily, it has become clear that ARCI should acquire or co-
develop technologies from other countries as well, if it has to maintain a sufficient number of technologies in its portfolio
 in the coming years.  With this aim a major programme on production & consolidation of nano powders has been initiated
 this year.
30.       The Department informed that during the current year emphasis would be given for completion and transfer of the
 technologies in Cold Spray Coating Technology, Electro Beam PVD Coating facility (EB-PVD), Diamond Like Coating
 facility (DLC), Micro Arc Oxidation Coating facility (MAO),Ceramic Honeycombs Programme and Stainless Steel &
 Titanium Filters.
31.       When the Committee asked the Department to explain the reasons for doubling the allocation from Rs.7.70 crores
 at B.E. and Rs.8.70 crores in R.E. stage in the year 2002-03 to Rs.15.00 crores in the year 2003-04 and the details of the
 programmes to be undertaken with the increased allocation, it was informed that the IARC, Hyderabad has over the years
 developed expertise in new materials for strategic use and it is now proposed to establish facilities for production of nano
 powders and Silicon Carbide (SiC) required for space applications and Indian industry and therefore additional grants
 have been sought for this purpose.
32.       The Committee commends the efforts of the Department for establishing the centre and hopes that its activities will
 give the country the desired results in a specified time frame.
TECHNOLOGY FOR BAMBOO PRODUCTS
33.
       The Committee was informed that while some of the national centres of excellence in India possess rich expertise
 in bamboo technology, the knowledge flow to the industry has not come up to the desired level.   As such it is high time to
 bring the technology sourcing avenues and industries for technology development transfer and commercialization.   Thus
 the aim is to undertake a programme at the national level which could impart a significant boost to the usage of bamboo,
 promote specialized products for commercialization and would generate good employment opportunities.
34.       The Planning Commission has taken a new initiative to additionally develop and support in the Tenth Plan, a range
 of bamboo related activities, and responsibilities.  A National Mission on Bamboo Applications(NMBA) has already been
 invested with increased activities.
35.       The basis for the increased allocation are the additional tasks and activity areas that have devolved on the NMBA,
 as a result of discussions with the Planning Commission.  The additional funds are, therefore, earmarked for:
a)            Demonstration of newly developed technologies, in the composites/ wood substitutes segment, and for structural
 application, agro-processing, grid reinforcement and soil stabilization.
b)            Development of product and application standards, testing and certification, market surveys and market
 promotion of new products, and preparation of manuals, codes of practice and technology dossiers.
The programme on technology for bamboo products is being designed more in the development-financing pattern
 while keeping the market acceptance, commercialization, and product branding as the ultimate objectives: The
 programme would be so designed that some seed capital could be provided on returnable basis to various identified sub-
projects aimed at specific product development activities.
While all the projects would necessarily be taken up in partnership with the industries, some may require a
 tripartite arrangement on knowledge share/transfer from academic/research institutions in India & abroad. The programme
 would also support technology transfer & absorption from advanced overseas sources towards domestic consumption and
 export opportunities. With certain technological maturity in the Indian system, the programme could encourage
 technology tie-ups & transfers from Indian industry to their counterparts in the developing world.
A provision of Rs. 43.25 crores has been proposed for the scheme during 2003– 04.

THE PHARMACEUTICALS RESEARCH AND DEVELOPMENT SUPPORT FUND (PRDSF)
40.       The emerging economic, trade and intellectual property scenario, nationally and internationally, necessitates a
 qualitative change in the industry, to drive Indian pharmaceutical industry away from manufacturing only known drugs to
 discovering and commercializing new molecules. The availability of trained scientific manpower of high quality, S&T
 infrastructure, accumulated knowledge of traditional medicinal system and large bio-diversity of our country offer a great
 opportunity to our industry. However, at present, most Indian drug firms, due to their small size compared to international
 operators and limited resources, are not in a position to invest in a viable new drug development programme. At the same
 time, several Indian academic institutions and national laboratories have established impressive infrastructure and
 developed excellent expertise in selected areas of drug development.
41.       The Committee was informed that the scheme aims at enhancing capabilities of the Indian drugs and
 pharmaceutical industry towards development of new drugs by synergising the strengths of publicly funded R&D
 institutions and the Indian Pharmaceutical drug industry for discovery and introduction of new drugs and practices in all
 systems of medicine.
42.       During the tenth plan the Department has a provision of Rs.150 Crores for the Pharmaceuticals Research and
 Development Support Fund (PRDSF).   This is the corpus fund.  The interest earned from this fund will be used for the
 purposes of supporting Research & Development (R&D) Programmes and setting up of the National facilities for
 furthering R&D activities in the country.  Since the interest on this corpus will be accrued only after a year, an initial
 budgetary support of Rs.10 crores has been provided for sustaining various activities during the financial year 2003-2004. 
 It is proposed to constitute a Drug Development Promotion Board to administer the fund.
43.       It was stated that under this scheme financial support would be provided to national labs and academic institutions
 for joint research programmes conceived by the industry and public funded R&D institutions. The broad objectives of this
 programme include: Development of new molecules and practices for diseases prevalent in the Indian climatic zone by
 bringing together the scientific expertise existing in the country in research institutions and industry; Promote R&D at any
 stage of development in all systems of medicine including alternative system of medicines and Creating state-of-the-art
 infrastructure facilities at par with international standards for the benefit of the Indian Industry and other users.
44.       The existing ongoing Plan Programme on Drug and Pharmaceuticals Research will be merged with this new
 activity.  The broad objectives of this fund are: -
1.         Funding research in all the systems of medicine in particular development of new molecules, natural products
 including plant, mineral and animal based preparations, development of new drug delivery systems,       application of
 genomics/proteomics and development of key chemicals/reagents used in drug research.
2.         To create an enabling infrastructure for promotion of R&D at all stages including clinical research.

 supporting collaborative projects for development of Drugs for various veterinary diseases during the period.

 points were taken up: Global Promotion of Ayurveda; Evaluation of different concepts and practice of ancient medical
 wisdom; Validation of evidence based research findings; Guidelines for standardization and quality control of herbal
 drugs; Patenting of original research source materials and  Strategies for obtaining FDA approval.   Based on the seminar

47.       A national Seminar on “Siddha Medicine” was held on December 9 & 10 at Tamil University, Thanjavur, with the
 purpose of holding an interaction meeting between R&D institutions and pharmaceutical industries.  There were six
 technical sessions during this seminar on, Industry institutional alliances, standardization of drugs, scientific
 validation/evaluation, prospective Siddha Drugs, Veterinary drugs, Siddha heritage. Nearly, 250 participants both from
 leading R&D institutions/academic/industries both from Central and States involved with Siddha medicine and related
 areas participated.  The Department informed the Committee that the following steps were suggested:
a)         The rich potential of Siddha Medicine buried in the Tamil literature like Tirumoolar Tirumandharam etc, the
 source book for Siddha Medicine has to be published in such a way it reaches the international community.
b)         The crude production of Siddha Medicine drugs has to be regulated in such a way that through study on the side
 effects on par with the studies on side effect from synthetic drugs.
c)         A well knit coordination and collaboration among the cultivators of the different raw materials for the Siddha
 drugs, micro-propagators of some industries, Department of Science and Technology, national laboratories and university
 departments involved in the development of Siddha Medicine has to be thought of.
d)         A well established universal nomenclature and methodology of naming the plants and development of well trained
 manpower to identify the different raw materials is considered to be the basic necessity.   Above all, it is also pointed out
 that a guide manual for identification of medicinal plants particularly to the industrialist has to be brought out at the
 earliest.
e)         There is a need to develop Siddha Drugs for killer diseases like HIV, cancer etc. through collaborative research
 project mode.

50.       The Committee was informed that the original objective of the Department was to build a center of excellence,
 which will have a focus on basic sciences, and would also develop a bias towards technology, keeping in line with
 international trends on liquid crystal materials and devices.   The infrastructure for research and development was
 strengthened to enlarge the scope of the research investigations.  This expansion is required to keep up with the
 international trends in this sector.  Modifications in the proposed plan will also be based on the needs of the industry as
 and when desired. The Centre was set up in 1985 as a society under the Department of Electronics but now this Centre has
 been transferred to the Department of Science & Technology.
51.            Highlighting the achievements made by the centre, the Committee was informed that a highly sophisticated
 magnetic suscepto-meter with super conducting pick up coils and SQUID to measure very low currents has been procured
 and installed.  This is the only such facility in the country, which is an important tool in characterizing many materials.
52.       It was further stated that the synthetic organic chemists of the Center form one of the leading groups, which has
 prepared a variety of new materials (both calamitic and discotic ) and some of the contributions by the group rank
 amongst the most accessed papers, as judged by the Journal of Materials Chemistry brought out by the Royal Institute of
 Chemistry.  This is an indication of the front line work being carried out at the Center.   The compounds have enormous
 potential applications as wide viewing angle, high contrast ratio and faster devices.
53.            Besides, the Centre carries out other major research studies, which include:
            a)   In another scientific work very high conductivity along the columnar axis of disc shaped molecule has already
 been achieved.   These can be thought of as analogous to molecular wires, using which one can envisage numerous
 applications like photoconductor, light emitting diodes, photovoltaic cells, etc.
            b)   Re-entrance of twist grain boundary mesophases that is analogous to the Abrikosov flux lattice phase in
 superconductors has been unambiguously proved.
c)      A novel example photoinduced disorder to order transition, which is contrary to the normal order to disordered

POPULARISATION OF SCIENCE
57.       The Committee was informed that the Department is making the children the real starting point for popularizing
 science and technology.   However, the Committee notes with concern that there are no laboratories and other
 infrastructure for promoting science among children.  The Department itself has informed the Committee that there is
 marked decline of interests among students to pursue science courses in our educational institutions.   To generate interest
 among students for science and scientific research, the Committee recommends that science cafes and children’s scientific
 parks may be established in rural and urban areas with local as well as corporate assistance.   Apart from this the
 Committee recommends that wide spread publicity must be given for the works done by our scientists and scientific
 institutions for making people aware about their achievements.   The Committee, therefore, recommends that the
 allocations at R.E. stage for all Departments dealing with science & technology may not be reduced.
